title: Labelled model paragraphs for each Component 1 section
subject: English Literature
source: Written for english-literature/y11 lesson 46 (Labelled model paragraphs for each Component 1 section (teacher-written, pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 46. One labelled model for each section. Find the move your weakest section is missing.

passage.title: Model
paras: The poet presents memory as something the body keeps when the mind has lost it. [claim] The grandmother's hands 'remember / what she has forgotten', [evidence] a paradox [method] that makes her skill feel almost separate from her, as if her fingers are wiser than her mind. [effect] The simile 'quick as prayer' suggests the movements are practised and faithful, so the reader feels both admiration and sadness. [effect on the reader]

passage.title: Model
paras: Both poets present a parent's love as something that must let go. [both poems, one claim] Where one speaker watches a child walk away, the other lets a father fade, yet in each poem the tone is tender rather than bitter. [comparative connective] Look closely at the final lines of your two poems: what each speaker gives up, and the single word that shows it. [method: zoom on both poems]
passage.byline: Model written for TGA (choose your own pair and quotations from the anthology)

blocks.h: Section C: Of Mice and Men

passage.title: Model
paras: Steinbeck uses Crooks to show that loneliness is made by society: kept in the harness room off the barn because of his race, he reflects the segregation of 1930s California, so Steinbeck turns one man's isolation into a criticism of injustice. [claim, evidence, context, purpose]

questions.q: From your analysis, write your weakest section and the main gap
questions.a: A section and a gap, e.g. 'Anthology: I write about one poem at a time.'

questions.q: Read the labelled model for your section and note the move you are missing
Core: in the portal response box, rewrite one paragraph from your weakest section to the next level using the model. Starter: '[Writer] presents...'
questions.a: A repaired paragraph showing the missing move clearly.

questions.q: Extend: write a timed (10-minute) paragraph for a second section
Stretch: add one precise context sentence to your prose paragraph
questions.a: A context sentence linked to purpose.

questions.q: A prose paragraph retells the plot well but has no argument. Best repair?
options: open with a claim about Steinbeck's purpose and use the plot as evidence
questions.a: A) open with a claim about Steinbeck's purpose and use the plot as evidence. The prose essay rewards argument and context, not retelling.

questions.q: Which section will you practise most this week?
Answer the ponder: which fix gains the most?
questions.a: A named fix with a reason.
